**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) Define any **TWO** of the following:

(i) Weathering,
(ii) Wind abrasion,
(iii) The long profile of a river.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two definitions, 2 marks each (all three are given here).

1. **Weathering** is the **breaking down (disintegration) or decay of rocks in their original place** (in situ) by the action of the weather (heat and cold, water, frost), plants, animals and chemical changes, with little or no movement of the broken material. Types: physical (mechanical) weathering, chemical weathering and biological weathering.
2. **Wind abrasion** is the **wearing away of rock surfaces by the sand and dust grains carried by the wind**, which hit the rock like sandpaper. It happens mainly in deserts and on dry coasts, and it can polish and undercut rocks (mushroom rocks, for example).
3. **The long profile of a river** is the **line (section) that shows the gradient of the river from its source to its mouth**, drawn as height against distance. It is usually a smooth concave curve: steep in the upper course, gentler in the middle course and almost flat near the mouth.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Briefly describe **THREE** evidences to show that the earth is spherical.
(ii) Briefly define the term Hydrological cycle.

(6+2=8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three evidences (6 marks, 2 marks each: the evidence and its short description).**

1. **Circumnavigation.** Ships and aircraft that travel continuously in one direction (for example westwards) come back to their starting point without turning back. This is possible only on a curved body such as a sphere (the first voyage round the world was completed by the expedition begun by Magellan in 1519-1522).
2. **Ships disappearing over the horizon.** A ship sailing away from the shore does not just get smaller: the hull disappears first and the mast is seen last, and a ship coming towards the shore shows the mast first. The curved surface of the sea hides the lower part of the ship.
3. **The shadow of the Earth on the Moon in a lunar eclipse** always has a curved, round edge, whatever the position of the Earth. Only a sphere always casts a round shadow.
4. **Other evidences (any can be used):** photographs from satellites and astronauts show a round Earth; the horizon is curved and widens as the observer climbs higher; time differs from place to place (time zones); different stars are seen when one moves north or south.

**(ii) Hydrological cycle (2 marks).** The hydrological cycle (water cycle) is the **continuous circulation of water between the sea, the atmosphere and the land**: water evaporates from the sea and the land (and is transpired by plants), condenses into clouds, falls as precipitation (rain, snow, hail) and returns to the sea by run-off, rivers and underground flow, and the cycle starts again.
themes: evidence for the earth's spherical shape

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Clearly state **TWO** problems created by each of the following:

(i) Poor waste management,
(ii) Water shortage (scarcity),
(iii) Floods,
(iv) Global warming.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two problems for each item, one mark per problem (8 marks).

**(i) Poor waste management**

1. **Diseases:** rubbish heaps and blocked gutters are breeding places for flies, rats and mosquitoes, which spread cholera, typhoid and malaria.
2. **Pollution and flooding:** waste thrown into drains and streams blocks them, pollutes the water and causes floods in towns when it rains. (Other answers: bad smells, burning of waste pollutes the air, soil pollution, ugly environment.)

**(ii) Water shortage (scarcity)**

1. **Diseases:** people use unsafe water from streams and shallow wells, which causes water-borne diseases such as cholera and typhoid, and poor hygiene.
2. **Loss of time and food:** women and children walk long distances to fetch water, and crops and livestock suffer or die, which leads to food shortage. (Other answers: conflicts over water, factories slow down.)

**(iii) Floods**

1. **Loss of life and property:** people and animals are drowned, and houses, roads, bridges and farms are destroyed.
2. **Hunger and disease:** crops are swept away or rot, causing food shortage, and floodwater spreads diseases (cholera, malaria). (Other answers: people are made homeless, soil erosion, pollution of water supplies.)

**(iv) Global warming**

1. **Rising sea level:** melting ice and warmer oceans make the sea rise and flood low coastal areas, islands and ports.
2. **Climate disturbance:** more droughts, desertification and violent storms, which reduce crop yields and cause food shortage (for example the shrinking of Lake Chad, to which climate change contributes). (Other answers: melting glaciers, spread of diseases, loss of species.)
